summary: Private deployment: SSO token aud check fails when customer ingress preserves Host header via identity-proxy, causing 403 to admin APIs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sudden 403 authorization failures for admin/operator endpoints in their private VPC deployment after a weekend ingress upgrade. Symptoms align with SSO-authenticated sessions failing authorization checks despite tokens appearing valid at the IdP side. Impact: Admin console and API calls that require elevated RBAC roles are blocked for multiple operators; day-to-day ops impaired. 

Observed behavior: Calls authenticated via Azure AD SSO succeed at token issuance but are rejected by Redwood private control-plane with an explicit audience mismatch message during token validation. Error started after customer applied an ingress change which enabled "preserveHost: true" on their identity-proxy service.

Why this matters: For private deployments we validate token audience (aud) strictly against expected runtime client IDs. Changes in the perceived host/origin can cause the auth-proxy to present a different effective audience during introspection/validation, leading to authorization denial even though the IdP issued a valid token to the user application.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer environment: private deployment behind identity-proxy, ingress change set preserveHost=true; Azure AD as IdP; admin API protected by requiring 'admin' RBAC binding.
2) Sign in via Azure AD, obtain id_token/access_token for the admin console (token appears issued without error).
3) Call admin API with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
4) Redwood private control-plane responds with 403 and logs an aud mismatch error during token validation.
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T08:12:04Z auth-validate ERROR token_validation.go:142 audience mismatch: expected 'redwood-private-prod' got 'api.finsight.com'
auth-proxy[pid=47] DEBUG proxy.go:223 forwarding original Host header: 'api.finsight.com'
idp-introspect response: active=true, scope='openid profile email', aud='api.finsight.com', azp='0000-aaaa-bbbb-cccc'
rbac-check WARN policy.go:87 principal resolved -> 'user:alice@finsight.com' roles:['admin-cust'] but aud check failed
investigation_notes: - Customer confirmed ingress upgrade on 2026-03-09 enabled preserveHost; rollback to previous config reproduced earlier behavior where requests pass.

- Token returned by Azure AD contains aud claim matching the external app identifier (api.finsight.com) instead of the internal Redwood client id ('redwood-private-prod'). The private control-plane validates aud strictly against configured accepted audiences.

- The identity-proxy is forwarding the original Host header and the downstream introspection flow is mapping incoming 'resource'/'aud' incorrectly when making local validation decisions. This only surfaces for tokens issued with audience equal to the customer's external app id.

- Similar issues in other customers were resolved by either adding the external audience to accepted audiences list or normalizing tokens in the proxy. Notable difference: customer does not want to modify IdP app registrations.
- Repro on staging by toggling preserveHost on the ingress results in the same aud mismatch and 403 responses.
workaround: Temporary workaround applied: support added the customer's external audience to the private control-plane accepted_audiences list for the customer's tenant (support action: /admin/tenants/fin_sight/set-accepted-audiences). This restored access for operators within 20 minutes. Customer requested a safer fix rather than a long-lived config workaround.
resolution: In progress — engineering to implement normalization in auth-proxy allowing an optional 'audience_aliases' mapping so tokens with the customer's external host audience can be accepted without adding the external app to tenant configuration. PR #2987 created; target hotfix rollout to dedicated/private customers by 2026-03-15. Long-term: update runbook and private deploy configuration docs to call out preserveHost implications for audience validation.
